followUp: Can you find the pair in less than O(n²) time?
hints: Brute force tries every pair. When nums[i] is fixed, what single value is it actually looking for?
For each x you need exactly target − x. What data structure answers "have I seen this value?" in O(1)?
Walk once with a map value → index. Check for the complement *before* storing the current number.

insight.mnemonic: Remember what you've passed; ask for the missing half.
insight.oneLiner: Don't search for pairs. For each x, ask one O(1) question: have I already seen target − x?

recall.a: Store value → index of everything seen so far; look up target − current.

insight.why: A pair (i, j) is found the moment you reach j, because nums[i] is already in the map. So one pass suffices: every pair is discovered at its second element.

pitfalls.explain: You returned the same index twice. Look up the complement *before* inserting the current number, or make sure the two indices differ.

pitfalls.explain: The answer is the two *positions*, not the two numbers.
pitfalls.title: Returned values instead of indices

pitfalls.explain: Sorting reorders positions. If you sort, sort (value, index) pairs - or use a hash map.
pitfalls.title: Sorted the array and lost the original indices

solutions.idea: Fix each index i and scan every j > i. Correct, but the inner scan repeats work: it re-reads the same numbers for every i.
solutions.name: Check every pair

footnotes.text: The whole trick: instead of searching for a pair, ask one O(1) question per element - have I already seen target - num?
Store *after* checking. Checking first means nums[i] can never pair with itself - the bug behind [3, 3] style failures.

solutions.idea: Trade memory for time. As you walk, store value → index. For each new number, the complement target − num is either already stored (pair found) or not yet seen.
solutions.name: One-pass hash map

class Solution:
    def twoSum(self, nums: List[int], target: int) -> List[int]:
statement:
You're given an integer array `nums` and an integer `target`. Find the **two different positions** whose values add up to `target`, and return their indices.

Every input has exactly one valid pair, and a position can't be paired with itself. The two indices may be returned in either order.
title: Two Sum
